scenes.text: How would you design society without knowing your own future place?
scenes.narration: Imagine you are chosen to rewrite all laws for society. But here is the catch: you do not know if you will be born rich or poor, healthy or sick!

scenes.text: Setting boundary rules before the toss decides whether you bat or bowl.
scenes.narration: Here is a simple cricket analogy. If you must set the boundary rules before the coin toss decides whether you bat or bowl, you will make the game completely fair.

scenes.name: John Rawls
scenes.idea: Justice as fairness is the first virtue of social institutions.
scenes.narration: John Rawls used this idea to revive political philosophy in 1971. He declared that justice is the first virtue of social institutions, just like truth is of thought.

scenes.heading: Priority of Right Over Good
scenes.narration: Rawls rejects utilitarianism, which sacrifices individual rights for the majority's happiness. Following Immanuel Kant, he insists right is prior to good: human dignity can never be traded away.

scenes.heading: The Path to Fair Rules
scenes.narration: Behind an imaginary Veil of Ignorance, you forget your wealth and talents. Not knowing your luck, you use the maximin rule: pick the rules where the worst possible outcome is safest.

scenes.heading: Lexical Order of Justice
scenes.narration: This gives three principles in strict priority. Equal liberty always comes first, fair equality of opportunity comes second, and economic inequalities are permitted only if they help the least advantaged.

scenes.heading: The Difference Principle
items: Natural talents are neither just nor unjust
Inequalities must benefit the least advantaged
Wealth is justified when helping the weakest
scenes.narration: Rawls explains that natural talents are pure luck, not moral merit. That is why greater wealth is fair only when it is shared to support the weakest section of society.

items: Justice as fairness protects inviolable human dignity
Veil of ignorance removes bias through maximin choice
Lexical order ensures liberty while supporting the weakest
scenes.narration: To recap: justice as fairness protects human dignity, the veil of ignorance eliminates personal bias, and the difference principle ensures society protects its most vulnerable.
